decisions.reason: Although it disappeared from website prominence, it began as a flagship tightly linked to the firm's announced cloud-messaging direction, so management is still inclined to justify the investment and treat disappointing traction as a repositioning or adoption-timing issue.

Because it builds on the firm's document-workflow capabilities and likely absorbed meaningful development effort, management is still somewhat prone to persist and explain weak visibility as bundling or sales-priority effects rather than a failed launch.
Its lower original prominence, adjacent rather than central strategic role, and continued absence from the website make it easier for management to stop defending and redeploy resources elsewhere.
As a narrow fax-related feature with limited public commitment and weaker fit with the firm's forward-looking innovation narrative, it is one of the easiest offers to withdraw.

Threat protection remains closely tied to the firm's secure and compliant positioning, so management has strong reputational and strategic reasons to continue and interpret weak standalone visibility as integration into the broader security stack.
